cur:objects-berlin-pyxis-two-healing-mir.summary: A youthful Christ, carrying a long cross-staff, strides toward a kneeling sick man and stretches out his hand to heal him, while apostles, one holding a jewelled book, follow behind. The deep, rounded carving gives the figures strong volume around the curve of the tusk. Boxes like this probably held the Eucharistic bread or relics, so that the images of healing surrounded what they contained.
facts: The museum attributes the pyxis to Egypt in the second half of the 6th century; Alexandria was a major centre of ivory carving in Late Antiquity (context).
cur:objects-berlin-pyxis-two-healing-mir.notes: The specific miracles are not identified in the accessible label.

walters:W.432.46R.summary: Christ hangs dead on the cross, crowned with green thorns and streaked with blood, against a golden evening sky. The Virgin, in a blue mantle, and John stand together at the left, while at the right a man in black kneels with joined hands, looking up at Christ. The miniature opens the Stabat Mater ('The sorrowful mother stood weeping beside the cross'), inviting the reader to join the kneeling figure in compassion.
facts: The miniature introduces the Stabat Mater among the prayers to the Virgin in this prayer book (fol. 46r).
The book was made in Leiden in the first quarter of the 16th century and contains Latin prayers and Gospel passages.

walters:W.432.46R.notes: Origin in Leiden and the date 1500–1525 follow the Walters manuscript description (TEI, The Digital Walters). The worklist year (800) was a parsing error for '1st quarter 16th century'. The identity of the kneeling man in black is not recorded.
